Subject: Processing addendum clarification + telemetry carveout

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Brightlane is excited about the latency profile and the private deployment option. Our legal team has one narrow but material ask on the DPA redline: they want to limit the telemetry Redwood collects for our instance to non-content operational metrics only (e.g., CPU/GPU, request counts, error codes) and exclude any request or prompt-level telemetry that could be reconstructed to infer PHI. They also want a 30-day maximum retention window for telemetry.

I've attached a redline (brightlane_dpa_redline_v3.pdf) that highlights the proposed carveout and a short telemetry matrix. Can you confirm whether those constraints are feasible from a product and security perspective? If needed we can accept a limited heartbeat/availability metric set for operational support but we need assurances about prompt content and retention.

Given this is a legal prerequisite for our procurement team, Brightlane will need Product and Security sign-off before procurement can proceed.

Quick win would be a short call among Product/Security/Legal to close scope. Are you available tomorrow morning PST?

Thanks,
Anna Park

Vanessa / team — quick technical readout from Product:

- Feasibility: Yes, for Dedicated/Private we can gate telemetry so that no prompt or request-level content is persisted outside ephemeral in-memory traces. We already support config flags that disable content-level logging; enabling that for Brightlane is straightforward.
- Retention: 30-day configurable retention for aggregated metrics is feasible; we currently default to 90 days in hosted but config is per-customer for Dedicated.
- Monitoring tradeoffs: removing request-level telemetry reduces our ability to do fine-grained regression detection (e.g., sudden semantic drift tied to prompts). Proposed compromise: provide a small set of hashed/ salted request fingerprints (one-way, non-reversible) plus service-level anomaly alerts. That preserves signal without exposing content.
- Engineering impact: low to medium. Need an ops task (~2 sprints) to add the retention toggle to the platform UI and to expand the pseudonymization pipeline for fingerprints. If Legal requires explicit wording around "non-reversible fingerprints" we should be precise about hashing/pepper and key rotation.

If Security and Legal are comfortable with the fingerprint approach, Product can sign off conditional on engineering delivering the retention toggle and pseudonymization implementation before GA. Happy to sketch the exact wording for the DPA.

—Markus
Markus Klein
Director, Product — Serving Runtime
markus.klein@redwood.com

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Processing addendum clarification + telemetry carveout

Thanks — high level Security feedback:

1) Telemetry scope: security is supportive of removing prompt-level telemetry from persistent stores. However we need the DPA to include: (a) explicit definitions of "telemetry" vs "operational logs", (b) a "no unredacted content" clause, and (c) a requirement that any derived fingerprints are one-way (cryptographic hash) with rotating salts managed in KMS/HSM.

2) Retention: 30 days is acceptable provided there is a documented retention policy and automated purge. We will need proof (test evidence) that purge jobs run as described before final sign-off.

3) Subprocessors: Brightlane asked to see a current subprocessor list. Legal should include standard subprocessor disclosures and a clause that Redwood will notify Brightlane of changes 30 days in advance for Dedicated/Private deployments.

4) Audit & incident language: require right-to-audit and incident notification SLA (48 hours initial notification). Also include that telemetry used for troubleshooting will be accessed only by named roles and logged in audit trails.

Dev/Laura — please redline the DPA with the proposed fingerprint wording and the KMS/HSM requirement. Markus — please add a short technical appendix (one page) describing the hashing scheme and the retention toggle behavior.

Hannah Schmitt
Head of Security Engineering
hannah.schmitt@redwood.com
